links.outcome: Distribution of clinically unsafe failure rates across medical specialties versus aggregate rankings
links.effect: Failures (<= -1 on Harmlessness and Accuracy) were unevenly distributed across specialties, creating domain-specific no-go zones hidden in aggregate rankings, even for highly ranked models.
links.quote: These failures are unevenly distributed across specialties, creating domain-specific ``no-go zones'' not visible in aggregate rankings or single-number leaderboards.

links.outcome: Whether pairwise preference metric reflects clinical safety performance of LLMs
links.effect: Preference is a poor proxy for safety; highly ranked models still had substantial rates of clinically meaningful failures (<= -1), and surface features explained slightly more preference variation than safety rubric differences.
links.quote: we find that clinician preference is a poor proxy for safety-critical performance.

unlisted_practices: Report safety-critical failure rates directly rather than relying on pairwise preference rankings
Clinically adjusted preference ranking combining pairwise preference with rubric-derived safety feedback

screen.reason: Evaluates clinician pairwise preference versus multi-criterion rubric safety evaluations across 13 LLMs and assesses an adjusted ranking methodology to detect safety-critical failures.
